content:
TOMISLAV MESARIĆ
Ulica Lipa 12, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia | +385 1 555 0142 | tomislav.mesaric@example.com

PROFESSIONAL PROFILE
Butcher with 9 years of experience in high-street and market butchery. Completed vocational butcher training and hold a current HACCP basic food hygiene certificate. Experienced in breaking down beef, pork and lamb, preparing meat for the counter, making fresh sausages, recording temperature checks and advising customers on cuts and cooking times.

CORE SKILLS
Carcass breakdown (beef, pork and lamb) | Cutting, boning, trimming and portioning | Fresh sausage making | Knife sharpening | Mincer and bandsaw operation | HACCP food hygiene | Cold-chain temperature checks | Customer service and product advice | Cash handling

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Butcher | Mesnica Kod Ante (family butcher shop), Zagreb
2019–Present
- Break down 2–3 beef forequarters and 10–12 pork sides each week; bone, trim and portion meat for the counter.
- Make four kinds of fresh sausage—ćevapi, kobasice, chipolata and lamb merguez—using the shop’s own recipes.
- Record cold-room (0–4 °C) and display-counter temperature checks twice daily.
- Serve about 120 customers on a typical Saturday, advising on cuts and cooking times.
- Train two apprentices in knife handling and cleaning routines.

Counter Assistant | Tržnica Dolac meat hall stall, Zagreb
2015–2019
- Served customers, weighed and priced orders, operated the till and completed cash-up.
- Cleaned and sanitised slicers, mincers and the counter at closing.

EDUCATION & CERTIFICATES
Vocational Certificate: Butcher (3-year programme) | Food Trades School Zagreb, 2015
HACCP Basic Food Hygiene Certificate | 2021; renewed 2024

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native) | English (good) | German (basic)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, professional CV with clear sections, relevant quantified achievements, and a very close match to the butcher/meat-counter role. The experience bullets demonstrate practical cutting, boning, trimming, portioning, sausage making, temperature recording, customer advice, equipment use, cash handling, and apprentice training. The figures—such as 2–3 beef forequarters, 10–12 pork sides, and approximately 120 Saturday customers—add credibility and impact. The document is comfortably within the requested two-page limit. No unsupported skills, qualifications, or experience were detected when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard headings, reverse-chronological experience, readable text, and strong role-specific keywords including butcher, carcass breakdown, beef, pork, lamb, boning, trimming, portioning, fresh sausage, HACCP, temperature checks, customer service, mincer, bandsaw, and cash handling. Its simple text-based formatting should parse reliably in most ATS systems. AI screening probability is high because the profile and skills closely reflect the advertised requirements and duties. A minor improvement would be to use the job advertisement's exact phrase "service counter" in the profile or skills section and to make the HACCP wording slightly more directly match "HACCP knowledge."
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document strongly aligns with the two must-have requirements and with the role's practical expectations. It shows fresh meat preparation for a counter, customer advice on cuts and cooking, HACCP temperature records, hygiene routines, equipment operation, and experience serving busy Saturday periods. It also supports FreshCart's stated priorities around knowledgeable service, hygiene, friendliness, reliability, and pride in practical work. The CV does not demonstrate packaging for self-service shelves, FIFO stock rotation, or maintaining a stated stock level at peak hours; these activities are not present in the Original Candidate Information and should not be added as facts. The candidate's two-month notice period is stated in the user's message but is not necessary to include in this CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/JOB-MATCH ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Profile section, change "preparing meat for the counter" to "preparing and portioning fresh meat for the service counter". This uses the job advertisement's terminology while remaining supported by the documented cutting, boning, trimming, and portioning experience.
2. In the Professional Profile or Core Skills section, change "HACCP food hygiene" to "HACCP knowledge and food hygiene" or "HACCP food hygiene and temperature checks" so the document directly matches the advertised requirement "HACCP knowledge" without overstating the candidate's qualification.
3. In the Core Skills section, consider changing "Customer service and product advice" to "Customer service, product advice and advice on cuts and cooking times". This makes the strongest customer-facing match more visible to ATS and recruiters, and it is directly supported by the experience section.
critique.critical_issues:
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "current HACCP basic food hygiene certificate"

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a concise, professional, highly relevant CV. It presents 9 years of directly relevant butchery and meat-counter experience, includes useful production volumes and customer numbers, and clearly demonstrates technical skills, hygiene practices, customer service, cash handling and apprentice training. The structure is easy to scan and comfortably within the requested two-page limit. The quantified achievements—such as breaking down 2–3 beef forequarters, 10–12 pork sides and serving approximately 120 Saturday customers—give the experience credibility and impact. No unsupported skills, qualifications or experience were identified when cross-referenced with the Original Candidate Information.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong. Standard section headings, reverse-chronological experience, clear job titles, plain text content and relevant keywords such as “butcher,” “HACCP,” “temperature checks,” “portioning,” “service counter,” “customer service,” “mincer” and “bandsaw” should parse reliably. The document has a high probability of passing an initial AI/ATS relevance screen because it directly matches both must-have requirements and uses terminology from the advert. For maximum targeting, the target job title could be added near the candidate’s name. Avoid placing the CV in a design-heavy template with columns, graphics, text boxes or icons.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is an excellent match for the role. Completed butcher training, more than 9 years of relevant experience, and HACCP knowledge are all clearly shown. The document also aligns well with the company’s emphasis on knowledgeable customer advice, hygiene, reliability and practical butchery skills. Fresh sausage production, carcass breakdown, counter service, temperature records and apprentice training are particularly strong evidence of fit. The advert’s forklift licence is a nice-to-have and is not present in the candidate information, so this remains a gap rather than a CV-writing defect. The CV does not evidence FIFO stock rotation, self-service shelf packaging or maintaining a specified peak stock level; these duties should not be added because they are not supported by the Original Candidate Information.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the header, directly below “TOMISLAV MESARIĆ,” add the target title “Butcher / Meat Counter Assistant.” This is truthful based on the documented butcher and counter-assistant experience and will improve immediate recruiter recognition and ATS matching. No other substantive changes are required.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, professional CV that is comfortably within the requested two-page limit. It presents relevant butcher experience clearly, uses measurable production volumes, and demonstrates practical skills in carcass breakdown, sausage making, temperature control, customer service and apprentice training. The structure is easy to scan, and the language is specific rather than generic. The main opportunity is to make the customer-service achievement in the original candidate information more prominent in the current-role experience section.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, clear chronological employment history, relevant job-title terminology, and strong keywords such as butcher, meat counter, HACCP, food hygiene, temperature checks, portioning, customer service, mincer and bandsaw. The use of pipe separators in the skills section should generally parse correctly, although simple bullet points would be slightly safer across older systems. AI screening probability is high because the document directly matches the required training, HACCP knowledge and meat-counter experience without unsupported claims.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is excellent. The CV shows both completed butcher training and substantially more than the required two years of meat-counter experience, as well as HACCP knowledge. It supports the role's core duties: cutting, boning, trimming, portioning, customer advice, temperature recording, cleaning and cash handling. The quantified sausage-making and carcass-breakdown experience is particularly relevant. It also reflects company culture signals around knowledgeable customer service, hygiene, reliability and pride in practical work. The nice-to-have forklift licence is not mentioned in the candidate information, so it remains an unconfirmed gap; it is not a defect in the CV and should not be implied. The CV also does not claim experience with FIFO stock rotation, self-service shelf packaging, or maintaining a 95% stock level, but the original candidate information does not establish those skills, so they should not be added.
critique.improvement_instructions:

MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENT — In the Core Skills section, replace the pipe-separated list with one skill per line using standard bullet points. Retain the existing wording, including “Carcass breakdown,” “Cutting, boning, trimming and portioning,” “HACCP knowledge and food hygiene,” and “Cold-chain temperature checks,” to preserve the strong keyword match while improving parsing consistency.
